user-code-on-own-domain-01.graded_text: The target layout serves people's HTML and JavaScript from a separate registrable domain, not from any subdomain of plinth.example.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:81 starts with "Move published apps to their own registrable domain, put it on the Public Suffix List" and then leaves an alternative open: "The other shape, putting `plinth.example` on the list and moving the product and session to another domain, keeps the brand on app addresses ... That's an owner call about the brand. Either way:". The alternative keeps user code on `<name>.plinth.example`, so the target layout never commits to a separate content domain. An option left for the owner does not count as chosen.

user-code-on-own-domain-02.graded_text: The reason given is that every subdomain of one registrable domain is the same site: script on a sibling subdomain can set cookies for the parent domain and ride same-site requests, which lets it interfere with sign-in (login CSRF or session confusion) or reach session tokens.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:7 "`<name>.plinth.example`, which is the same site (same registrable domain) as `app.plinth.example`"; :10 "`SameSite=Lax/Strict` does not stop a published app from sending forged requests (CSRF)"; :11 "Any published app can set a `Domain=plinth.example` cookie. Browsers then send that cookie to `app.plinth.example`. A published app can use this to log a visitor into the attacker's session"; :9 covers reading the session token when a cookie is readable by script.

user-code-on-own-domain-03.graded_text: The short <name>.plinth.example address is kept as Plinth's own page, which frames the app served from the other domain, so visitors still see the Plinth address.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:81 moves the short address to the new domain: "keep the addresses short: `<name>.<short-user-domain>`". :84 then says to use "permanent redirects that keep path and query" off the old origin. Nothing keeps `<name>.plinth.example` as a Plinth-owned page that frames the app. I checked hosting-plan.md and answer.txt and found no iframe or outer page.

user-code-on-own-domain-04.graded_text: Each app gets its own origin on the content domain, such as a label per app, so one app cannot read another's storage.

votes.e: B/project/docs/hosting-plan.md:81 "`<name>.<short-user-domain>`. Then each app is its own site, `SameSite` and cookie scoping work as designed". This is one label per app on a PSL-listed content domain, and :15 notes each app's own origin keeps `localStorage` separate.

user-code-on-own-domain-05.graded_text: Until the separate domain can be set up after the freeze, people's code runs with an opaque origin, through a sandbox (for example a CSP sandbox header) without allow-same-origin, and the plan says this costs the apps their browser storage. It does not keep serving people's code as the top-level document on plinth.example subdomains during the beta.
